In the absence of telephones which are installed directly into the cell, there is no direct means for a prisoner to contact the Samaritans. In the event that a prisoner does not have access to a telephone they are reliant on staff to convey them to a telephone so they may call. There is a particular difficulty in respect of prisoners who are deemed to pose a risk of violence and who may not be able to immediately access a telephone, a listener or a member of Chaplaincy
lack of direct telephone access for prisoners to contact Samaritans

Prison Officers are not routinely briefed as to prisoners who have previously significantly self harmed in custody. It is not clear as to the threshold of severity required before prison staff will be informed save that they will be informed if a prisoner arrives with an open ACCT. Prison Officers are not routinely briefed as to a prisoner's previous or antecedent pattern of thoughts, feelings, events and behaviours which have led to incidents of significant self-harm
lack of routine briefing on prisoners' history of significant self-harm
